segmentation.text: A person
shall not stop, stand or park a vehicle,
except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic
or in compliance with law
or the directions of a police officer
or official traffic-control device,
in any of the following places:
Except as otherwise provided in subsection 3,
on a sidewalk.

A person may park a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter on a sidewalk provided that the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter does not impede the normal and reasonable movement of pedestrians on the sidewalk.

elements.justification: 'A person' who stops, stands or parks a vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading): the binder is the vehicle, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; same mapping as the index row 'A person'.

'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate. 'stop, stand or park' together denote every halt: DEF-NRS-484A-260 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not', DEF-NRS-484A-250 'the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not', DEF-NRS-484A-155 'the standing of a vehicle'; the exclusion of DEF-NRS-484A-260 is the law's own exception (b3-b6), and those of standing and parking (passengers, loading) are covered by stopping, so the union is drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation') with p.halt_speed_tolerance. Same mapping as the index row 'No person shall stop, stand or park a vehicle'.

Nearest atoms only, shown to mark the gap: a halt a governing dev.stop_sign or red dev.traffic_signal requires of a travel region the subject occupies (dev.governs, rel.occupies, st.travel_region) is one halt in compliance with law, but 'law' also requires halts no device shows (yielding to oncoming traffic before a turn, to an emergency vehicle, to a school bus), and the formula language composes only named rules (rule, ruleApplies), never whether some engaged rule of the set requires the halt. Same atoms as the index row 'in compliance with law'; the words carry operator gap smoke31-1111-0039:G22.

DEF-NRS-484A-180 'every officer authorized to direct or regulate traffic': dev.human_direction 'a person directing traffic and the direction given; role ... police_officer; indication ... stop', governing (dev.governs) a travel region the subject occupies. Same atoms as the index row 'or the directions of a police officer'.

DEF-NRS-484A-145 'every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority or railroad for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic': the devices whose direction requires a halt -- dev.stop_sign, dev.yield_sign, dev.traffic_signal with a red indication, dev.railway_signal_or_gate with lights flashing or gate lowering or down -- governing (dev.governs) a travel region the subject occupies. 'official' is the legal status of the device, read from its presence (status reading). Same atoms as the index row 'or a traffic control device,'.

st.sidewalk is the 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line' (DEF-NRS-484A-240 'that portion of a highway between the curb lines or the lateral lines of a highway and the adjacent property lines intended for the use of pedestrians'); it is not a stand-in for a crosswalk, which the words do not name. rel.occupies anchors the subject's footprint on it.

operationalizations.standard: necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic
operationalizations.convention: a halt is necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic where a road user of traffic is ahead of the halted vehicle in the same lane within the body gap of a queue of halted vehicles

residues.why: Bicycles, electric bicycles and electric scooters are no vehicles under DEF-NRS-484A-320 ('except: (1) Devices moved by human power ... (2) Electric bicycles ... (4) An electric scooter'), so the subject of this duty is never one of them and the duty is the same whether or not the words of subsection 3 hold.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle. Engaged at an observation where the subject occupies (rel.occupies) an st.sidewalk region and none of the exceptions holds there: no other road user of any class (DEF-NRS-484A-285 'traffic' counts 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances') is ahead of the subject in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with rel.surface_gap at most p.queue_halt_gap; the subject occupies no st.travel_region governed (dev.governs) by a dev.stop_sign, a dev.yield_sign, a dev.traffic_signal showing circular_red, red_arrow or flashing_red, or a dev.railway_signal_or_gate with lights flashing or gate lowering or down; no dev.human_direction of role police_officer indicating stop governs a travel region it occupies; and the halt is not one in compliance with law (operator gap on b4).
obligation: drv.motion.complete_halt(subject; p.halt_speed_tolerance) does not hold: the subject is not at rest while on the sidewalk. A halt there is violated.

narrowings.why: 'A person' who stops, stands or parks a vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever controls it.

'necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic' is read only as a halt behind a road user ahead in the same lane within the queue gap; a halt for a crossing road user that is not ahead in the lane is not read as excused.
'official traffic-control device' is read from the device's presence on the road, its official status presumed.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject car halts with its front half on a sidewalk across a driveway for 30 s; no road user ahead of it, no device or officer governs the region it occupies; no other road user in the scene.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The subject car crosses a sidewalk at a driveway at 3 m/s without halting.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject car halts in the roadway lane, its footprint overlapping no sidewalk.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject car is on a sidewalk across a driveway, but kin.speed is not observed on this source, so whether it is at rest is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject car halts with part of its body on the sidewalk while a police officer's stop direction governs the lane it also occupies.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The subject car halts with part of its body on the sidewalk 2 m behind a halted car ahead of it in the same lane.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
shall not make a U-turn
in a business district,
except at an intersection
or on a divided highway
where an appropriate opening or crossing place exists.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom; ru.aggregate 'true when the user carries an included class'. 'The driver of' is the relational role DEF-NRS-484A-080 defines ('every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle'), which the aggregate is not a stand-in for: it is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading), so the binder is the vehicle whose conduct is judged. Same mapping as the index row 'The driver of a vehicle'.

drv.motion.u_turn denotes a road user that 'has turned "so as to proceed in the opposite direction": its heading has reversed, "whether accomplished by one continuous movement or not"', the definition DEF-NRS-484B-077 ('the turning of a vehicle upon a highway so as to proceed in the opposite direction, whether accomplished by one continuous movement or not'). The concept 'says nothing of the way on which a turns', so the definition's 'upon a highway' is carried beside it: rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') of an st.highway region ('the entire public way between its boundary lines'); st.highway is not a stand-in for the roadway, and the definition names the highway, not the roadway. The index maps 'shall not make a U-turn' to drv.motion.u_turn alone; the highway anchor is added here because the defined word carries it (PLAN.md).

st.intersection: 'the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges; a junction where an alley meets another way ... is no intersection', matching DEF-NRS-484A-105 ('the area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines ... The junction of an alley with a street, road or highway shall not constitute an intersection'). It is not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line, which the words do not name. rel.occupies anchors the subject's own intersection: 'at an intersection' is the reversal made with the footprint overlapping it.

DEF-NRS-484A-070: 'a highway divided into two or more roadways by means of a physical barrier or dividing section'. st.median_or_divider is the 'physical barrier or dividing section between roadways'; st.on_way ties it to 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on'; rel.occupies anchors the subject on that st.highway. Same mapping as the index row 'driven upon a divided highway'. st.on_way is not a stand-in for nearness: the divider lies on the very way the subject occupies.

st.median_or_divider carries an 'opening attribute where a crossover exists': the opening or crossing place in the divider. rel.occupies of a divider region having that attribute is the reversal passing through the crossover. Same atoms as the index row 'except through an opening in the barrier or dividing section or space'. 'appropriate' is the legal status of a feature on the road: the opening's presence is its evidence (observable_reading, status).

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle). The rule is engaged at an observation where the reading declares asm.business_district for the subject's place there; for a reversal of direction, at the observation at which the reversal is recognized.
obligation: At the observation at which drv.motion.u_turn(subject; window p.vehicle_turn_window, u_turn_min p.u_turn_heading_min, yaw_tol p.turn_yaw_rate_tol) rises while the subject occupies (rel.occupies) an st.highway region, one of the exceptions holds, else violated: (a) at every observation while the reversal is under way the subject occupies an st.intersection region; or (b) at every observation while it is under way the subject occupies an st.highway region on which (st.on_way) an st.median_or_divider region lies, and at some observation while it is under way the subject's footprint overlaps an st.median_or_divider region on that highway having the opening attribute. Where no reversal is recognized the duty is complied with.

narrowings.why: 'The driver of a vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle whoever or whatever controls it.

'an appropriate opening or crossing place' is read by the presence of a divider region carrying the opening attribute on the divided highway the subject occupies; its legal suitability is presumed from that presence.

under_way.justification: kin.yaw_rate is the 'rate of change of heading'; its magnitude above p.turn_yaw_rate_tol tells an observation inside the reversal from one before it began, when the vehicle ran straight on the same region. It is a reading of the road user's motion, not of a place.

param_proposals.name: p.vehicle_turn_window
param_proposals.convention: the longest duration of a turn by a motor vehicle at a junction or into or out of a driveway, from the start of its heading change to its end, including the crossing of opposing lanes
param_proposals.source: observed turning-manoeuvre durations of passenger cars at urban junctions

param_proposals.name: p.u_turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change magnitude over the turn window at which a turn counts as a reversal of direction
param_proposals.source: geometric convention separating a turn (about 90 degrees) from a reversal (about 180 degrees)

param_proposals.name: p.turn_yaw_rate_tol
param_proposals.convention: the yaw-rate magnitude at or below which a road user's heading counts as no longer turning: the yaw-rate noise floor of the source
param_proposals.source: yaw-rate noise of vehicle inertial and tracking sources

segmentation.text: A vehicle
shall not be turned so as to proceed in the opposite direction
upon any curve,
or upon the approach to or near the crest of a grade,
where such vehicle cannot be seen by the driver of any other vehicle approaching from either direction within 500 feet.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, one atom; same mapping as the index row 'A vehicle'.

drv.motion.u_turn denotes a road user that 'has turned "so as to proceed in the opposite direction": its heading has reversed', the very words of the span; the reversal 'whether accomplished by one continuous movement or not' is denoted. 'be turned' by the one at the controls is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading).

st.curvature is the 'horizontal curvature of the roadway at a point, as a magnitude (1/m, never negative): a bend to either hand has the same value'; 'any curve' names the feature without a size, so it is read as the curvature at the subject's place standing clear of zero, above p.curvature_resolution, which names only the source's resolution. rel.occupies of an st.roadway region ('the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic') anchors the curve to the way the subject is upon. st.curvature is the road's geometry, not the vehicle's yaw (kin.yaw_rate is 'not a stand-in for road curvature').

st.crest is 'the place on a roadway's longitudinal profile where the slope changes from rising to falling in the direction of travel, carried as a region with a reference point and a boundary, so the ground distance from a road user to it is read through st.region_geometry' -- 'the crest of a grade'. st.region_geometry gives 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it'; the approach to or nearness to the crest is that distance at most p.crest_near_reach. st.crest is not a stand-in for the slope at a point (st.grade) nor for the view (st.sight_distance), which s5 reads on its own.

st.sight_distance is 'the distance along the road within which a vehicle at a point and another vehicle on the road could see each other ... both the view of approaching traffic from that point and its being seen by drivers approaching it, whether or not any road user is there': 'such vehicle cannot be seen by the driver of any other vehicle approaching from either direction within 500 feet' is that distance at the subject's place below 500 ft. It is not a stand-in for whether an actual road user saw another (rel.visible): the words state what could be seen at the place, whether or not another vehicle is present, so no other vehicle is quantified (perception reading).

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle). The rule is engaged at an observation where, at that one observation, (i) the subject occupies an st.roadway region and st_curvature at its place exceeds p.curvature_resolution, or the ground distance (st.region_geometry) from its body to an st.crest region is at most p.crest_near_reach; and (ii) st.sight_distance at its place is below 500 ft. For a reversal of direction, it is engaged where (i) and (ii) hold together at some one observation while the reversal is under way (yaw rate magnitude above p.turn_yaw_rate_tol, within the act's window behind its recognition).
obligation: drv.motion.u_turn(subject; window p.vehicle_turn_window, u_turn_min p.u_turn_heading_min, yaw_tol p.turn_yaw_rate_tol) does not rise: a reversal recognized where the rule is engaged is a violation; otherwise complied with.

narrowings.why: 'be turned' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever is at the controls.

'cannot be seen by the driver of any other vehicle approaching from either direction' is read through the sight distance of the subject's place (what could be seen at a place), not through any actual driver's perception.

segmentation.text: A person,
except when stopping, standing or parking where no parking is permitted,
shall not start a vehicle which is stopped, standing or parked on a highway
nor enter upon a highway
unless and until such movement can be made with safety.

elements.justification: 'A person' who starts a vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading), so the binder is the vehicle, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; same mapping as the index row 'A person'.

'stopping, standing or parking' (DEF-NRS-484A-260 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle'; DEF-NRS-484A-250 'the halting of a vehicle'; DEF-NRS-484A-155 'the standing of a vehicle') together denote every halt, drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation'), read at the observation before the start. 'where no parking is permitted' is a place a no-parking restriction marks: an st.curb_zone of kind no_parking, no_stopping or fire_lane or a curb painted red, which the vehicle's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies), or an st.travel_region it occupies that a dev.regulatory_sign of code no_parking, no_standing or no_stopping governs (dev.governs) with its conditions holding (prim.conditions_hold). The sign is a condition, not a manoeuvre (its not-a-stand-in clause does not apply); the posted or painted feature is the evidence of the restriction (status reading).

'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate. 'stopped, standing or parked' is every halt (the three definitions' union: DEF-NRS-484A-260 'any halting, even momentarily', DEF-NRS-484A-250 'the halting of a vehicle', DEF-NRS-484A-155 'the standing of a vehicle'; their exclusions -- conflict or device halts, passenger and loading halts -- intersect only on purposes no conduct shows), drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance. 'start' is the observation at which complete_halt ceases to hold, having held at the previous one. 'on a highway' is rel.occupies of an st.highway region ('the entire public way between its boundary lines', matching DEF-NRS-484A-095 'the entire width between the boundary lines'), at the previous observation.

operationalizations.standard: such movement can be made with safety
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a movement is made with safety where, at its onset, no other road user's centre is predicted under constant velocities to come within the conflict centre clearance of the subject's centre within the time-to-collision horizon

applicability: The subject is a vehicle. Engaged at an observation at which the subject starts: drv.motion.complete_halt(subject; p.halt_speed_tolerance) held at the previous observation while the subject occupied an st.highway region, and does not hold at this observation; and the exception does not hold: at the previous observation the subject did not occupy a place where no parking is permitted -- an st.curb_zone of kind no_parking, no_stopping or fire_lane, or one whose curb colour is red, or an st.travel_region governed (dev.governs) by a dev.regulatory_sign of code no_parking, no_standing or no_stopping whose conditions hold (prim.conditions_hold).
obligation: At that observation no other road user of the scene, of any class (same excludes the subject), satisfies prim.closest_approach_within(subject, other; p.conflict_horizon) with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, other; p.conflict_horizon) at or below p.conflict_centre_clearance. Where one does, violated.

narrowings.why: 'A person' who starts a vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle, whoever or whatever controls it.

'where no parking is permitted' is read by the posted no-parking, no-standing or no-stopping sign whose conditions hold, or the marked or red-painted curb zone, the feature's presence being the evidence of the restriction.

'with safety' is read only as the absence, at the onset of the movement, of a predicted near-collision with another road user; 'unless and until' is read at the start observation, the start being withheld until then.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject car stands at the curb on a highway for 20 s, outside any no-parking zone, then starts (speed rises above the tolerance) while another car 12 m behind it in the same lane closes at 12 m/s, so their centres are predicted to meet within the horizon.

scenarios.narrative: The subject car stands at the curb on a highway and starts; no other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: idle

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject car halted in a curb zone of kind no_parking painted red starts while another car 12 m behind closes at 12 m/s: the exception holds.

segmentation.text: A person,
except when stopping, standing or parking where no parking is permitted,
shall not start a vehicle which is stopped, standing or parked on a highway
nor enter upon a highway
unless and until such movement can be made with safety.

elements.justification: 'A person' who enters upon a highway with a vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading): the binder is the vehicle, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; same mapping as the index row 'A person'.

'stopping, standing or parking' (DEF-NRS-484A-260 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle'; DEF-NRS-484A-250 'the halting of a vehicle'; DEF-NRS-484A-155 'the standing of a vehicle') together denote every halt, drv.motion.complete_halt, read at the observation before the entry. 'where no parking is permitted': an st.curb_zone of kind no_parking, no_stopping or fire_lane or a curb painted red that the footprint overlaps (rel.occupies), or an st.travel_region it occupies governed (dev.governs) by a dev.regulatory_sign of code no_parking, no_standing or no_stopping whose conditions hold (prim.conditions_hold); the posted or painted feature is the evidence (status reading).

'enter upon a highway' is the observation at which the subject's footprint comes to overlap (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') an st.highway region ('the entire public way between its boundary lines', DEF-NRS-484A-095 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way'), having overlapped no highway region at the previous observation. st.highway is not a stand-in for the roadway: the words name the highway.

operationalizations.standard: such movement can be made with safety
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a movement is made with safety where, at its onset, no other road user's centre is predicted under constant velocities to come within the conflict centre clearance of the subject's centre within the time-to-collision horizon

applicability: The subject is a vehicle. Engaged at an observation at which the subject enters upon a highway: it occupies an st.highway region here and occupied none at the previous observation; and the exception does not hold: at the previous observation the subject was not at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance) in a place where no parking is permitted -- an st.curb_zone of kind no_parking, no_stopping or fire_lane or whose curb colour is red, or an st.travel_region governed (dev.governs) by a dev.regulatory_sign of code no_parking, no_standing or no_stopping whose conditions hold (prim.conditions_hold).
obligation: At that observation no other road user of the scene, of any class (same excludes the subject), satisfies prim.closest_approach_within(subject, other; p.conflict_horizon) with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, other; p.conflict_horizon) at or below p.conflict_centre_clearance. Where one does, violated.

narrowings.why: 'A person' who enters upon a highway is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle, whoever or whatever controls it.

'where no parking is permitted' is read by the posted no-parking, no-standing or no-stopping sign whose conditions hold, or the marked or red-painted curb zone, the feature's presence being the evidence of the restriction.

'with safety' is read only as the absence, at the entry, of a predicted near-collision with another road user; 'unless and until' is read at the entry observation, the entry being withheld until then.

segmentation.text: A driver
shall not stop
or suddenly decrease the speed
of a vehicle
without first giving an appropriate signal
to the driver of any vehicle immediately to the rear.

elements.justification: 'A driver' is the relational role of DEF-NRS-484A-080, read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading): the binder is the vehicle, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; same mapping as the index row 'a driver'.

'stop' is here a stopping the clause prohibits, so DEF-NRS-484A-260 applies ('when prohibited, any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle'): the onset of drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation'), the observation at which it holds and did not at the previous one. The definition's exclusion, which the concept does not make, is carried beside it: 'except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic' -- a road user ahead in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, 'a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane') within p.queue_halt_gap of body gap (rel.surface_gap, 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies'); 'or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device' -- the subject occupies (rel.occupies) an st.travel_region governed (dev.governs) by a dev.stop_sign, a dev.yield_sign, a dev.traffic_signal showing a red indication, a dev.railway_signal_or_gate flashing or with gate lowering or down, or a dev.human_direction of role police_officer indicating stop. dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position; it reads which device controls the region occupied.
'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, the subject's class.

The signal of a stop or a decrease of speed is the brake lamp ('brake lamps lit') or the arm signal (sig.hand_signal, 'meaning ... stop_or_slow'). sig.brake_lamp is not a stand-in for a halt or a deceleration, and is not used as one: the halt and the deceleration are read from kinematics, the lamp only as the signal other road users see. 'first' is read as shown at the onset of the halt or the deceleration or at some observation of the window of length p.stop_signal_lead_window behind it.

'any vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, read on the other road user; 'immediately to the rear' is that road user behind the subject in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, 'a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction') with the gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap) at most p.rear_signal_reach. rel.surface_gap is not a stand-in for an order of arrival; the order is read from rel.ahead_behind_in_lane. 'the driver of' is read through that vehicle (agency); no perception by that driver is read.

operationalizations.convention: a decrease of speed is sudden where the longitudinal deceleration exceeds the comfortable deceleration most drivers use when braking for an expected stop

applicability: The subject is a vehicle. Engaged at an observation E at which either (a) drv.motion.complete_halt(subject; p.halt_speed_tolerance) holds and did not hold at the previous observation, and that halt is not excused under DEF-NRS-484A-260: no road user is ahead of the subject in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with rel.surface_gap at most p.queue_halt_gap, and the subject occupies no st.travel_region governed (dev.governs) by a dev.stop_sign, a dev.yield_sign, a dev.traffic_signal showing circular_red, red_arrow or flashing_red, a dev.railway_signal_or_gate with lights flashing or gate lowering or down, or a dev.human_direction of role police_officer indicating stop; or (b) the subject's kin.accel_longitudinal is at or below minus p.sudden_decel_min and was not at the previous observation; and at E some other road user of the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle is behind the subject in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with rel.surface_gap at most p.rear_signal_reach.
obligation: At E, or at some observation of the time window of length p.stop_signal_lead_window behind E, the subject showed sig.brake_lamp lit or a sig.hand_signal meaning stop_or_slow. Otherwise violated.

narrowings.why: 'A driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle, whoever or whatever controls it.
'an appropriate signal' is read as the brake lamps lit or the stop-or-slow arm signal; 'first' as shown at the onset or within the lead window behind it.

segmentation.text: Upon any highway
outside of a business or residence district
no person shall stop, park or leave standing any vehicle,
whether attended or unattended,
upon the paved or main-traveled part of the highway
when it is practicable to stop, park or so leave such vehicle off such part of the highway,
but in every event an unobstructed width of the highway opposite a standing vehicle shall be left
for the free passage of other vehicles
and a clear view of such stopped vehicles shall be available from a distance of 200 feet in each direction upon such highway.

This section shall not apply to the driver of any vehicle which is disabled while on the paved or main-traveled portion of a highway in such manner and to such extent that it is impossible to avoid stopping and temporarily leaving such disabled vehicle in such position.

elements.justification: st.highway is 'the entire public way between its boundary lines' (DEF-NRS-484A-095 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way'); rel.occupies anchors the subject on it. Same mapping as the index row 'on any highway'.

'any vehicle' is the admitted aggregate. 'stop, park or leave standing' together denote every halt: DEF-NRS-484A-260 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not', DEF-NRS-484A-250 'the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not', DEF-NRS-484A-155 'the standing of a vehicle'; their exclusions (a halt to avoid conflict or on a device's direction; one receiving or discharging passengers; one loading) intersect only on purposes no conduct shows, so the union is drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation') with p.halt_speed_tolerance. 'no person' is read through the vehicle's conduct (agency).

st.roadway is 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder': the paved or main-traveled part. The roadway is not a stand-in for the sidewalk, and 'not on the roadway' includes the shoulder, which is the place off that part the words contrast it with. rel.occupies anchors the subject's footprint on it.

Nearest atoms only, shown to mark the gap: kin.engine_running is 'not a stand-in for motion or a halt' and an engine stopped does not make a vehicle unable to move; sig.hazard is a signal a road user emits, not the condition of the vehicle. Neither denotes a vehicle disabled so that it is impossible to avoid stopping; the span is filed as an atom gap.

operationalizations.standard: practicable to stop, park or so leave such vehicle off such part of the highway
operationalizations.convention: leaving a vehicle off the main-traveled part is practicable where a shoulder or a parking bay lies on the same way within the distance a vehicle covers when braking from a rural speed at a comfortable deceleration

residues.why: The duty is the same whether or not a person is with the vehicle: the words say so expressly.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle. Engaged at an observation where the subject occupies an st.highway region, the reading does not declare asm.business_or_residence_district for its place (declared false), the subject occupies an st.roadway region, and an st.shoulder or st.parking_space region lies on the same highway (st.on_way) within ground distance (st.region_geometry) p.offroad_refuge_reach of the subject's body. Not engaged where the subject is disabled so that it is impossible to avoid stopping (gap).
obligation: drv.motion.complete_halt(subject; p.halt_speed_tolerance) does not hold: the subject is not at rest on the roadway. A halt there is violated.

narrowings.why: 'no person shall stop, park or leave standing' is read through the vehicle's conduct, whoever controls it.
'practicable' is read as the presence of a shoulder or bay on the same way within the reach; whether that place is occupied or wide enough is not read.

segmentation.text: Upon any highway
outside of a business or residence district
no person shall stop, park or leave standing any vehicle,
whether attended or unattended,
upon the paved or main-traveled part of the highway
when it is practicable to stop, park or so leave such vehicle off such part of the highway,
but in every event an unobstructed width of the highway opposite a standing vehicle shall be left
for the free passage of other vehicles
and a clear view of such stopped vehicles shall be available from a distance of 200 feet in each direction upon such highway.

This section shall not apply to the driver of any vehicle which is disabled while on the paved or main-traveled portion of a highway in such manner and to such extent that it is impossible to avoid stopping and temporarily leaving such disabled vehicle in such position.

elements.justification: st.highway is 'the entire public way between its boundary lines' (DEF-NRS-484A-095); rel.occupies anchors the subject on it. Same mapping as the index row 'on any highway'.
st.roadway is 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder': the paved or main-traveled part; rel.occupies anchors the subject's footprint on it.

'a standing vehicle' is the subject (admitted aggregate) at rest, drv.motion.complete_halt (DEF-NRS-484A-250 'the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not'). 'an unobstructed width of the highway opposite' is the free width across the roadway beside its body: prim.region_lateral_offset ('the signed lateral offset ... of a structure region from a road user') to the st.road_edge ('curb or edge of the roadway') on the same way (st.on_way) on the side away from the curb it stands at, less half its width (kin.extent, 'a formula reads the full length, width and height'), with no st.obstruction region and no halted other road user (rel.occupies of the roadway) within that width beside it (st.region_geometry). 'shall be left' by the person is read through the vehicle's position (agency).

Nearest atoms only, shown to mark the gap: kin.engine_running is 'not a stand-in for motion or a halt'; sig.hazard is a signal, not the vehicle's condition. Neither denotes a disabled vehicle; filed as an atom gap.

operationalizations.standard: the free passage of other vehicles
operationalizations.convention: a width is left for free passage where the unobstructed lateral width of roadway beside the standing vehicle is at least the width one passing design vehicle needs with its lateral clearance, about a narrow traffic lane

residues.why: The duty is the same whether or not a person is with the vehicle: the words say so expressly.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle. Engaged at an observation where the subject occupies an st.highway region, asm.business_or_residence_district is declared false for its place, and the subject is at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance) occupying an st.roadway region, whether or not it is practicable to leave it elsewhere. Not engaged where the subject is disabled so that it is impossible to avoid stopping (gap).
obligation: The lateral width from the subject's body to the st.road_edge region on the same way on its open side (prim.region_lateral_offset, less half the subject's width from kin.extent) is at least p.free_passage_width, and no st.obstruction region and no other halted road user lies within that width beside the subject. Otherwise violated.

narrowings.why: 'shall be left' is read through the standing vehicle's position on the roadway, whoever placed it; 'opposite' is read as beside the vehicle across the roadway on the side away from the edge it stands nearest.
'free passage of other vehicles' is read as a lateral width at least one passing design vehicle's width with clearance; the passage of wider vehicles is not separately read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: District declared false; the subject car stands in the roadway of a narrow rural road with the far road edge 2 m beyond its body.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: District declared false; the subject car stands at the right edge of a wide roadway leaving 6 m of clear roadway beside it; no obstruction and no other road user.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: District declared false; the subject car drives along the roadway at 20 m/s and never stands.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: District declared false; the subject car stands in the roadway, but st.region_geometry is not observed on this source, so the free width cannot be measured.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of tracking sources

param_proposals.name: p.free_passage_width
param_proposals.convention: the free lateral width one passing vehicle needs beside a standing vehicle: the width of a design passenger or single-unit vehicle with its lateral clearance, about a narrow traffic lane
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book design vehicle widths and minimum lane width

gaps.proposal: `ru.disabled` | the vehicle cannot move under its own power (a breakdown, damage, a flat tyre), as the source records it **Not a stand-in for:** a vehicle at rest with its engine stopped, or one showing hazard lamps -- the condition is not a halt and not a signal | general
gaps.nearest: kin.engine_running (Not a stand-in for: motion or a halt -- a vehicle stands with its engine running and rolls with it stopped; an engine off is not a vehicle unable to move); sig.hazard (a signal a road user emits, not the vehicle's condition)

st.roadway is 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder': the paved or main-traveled part; rel.occupies anchors the subject's footprint on it.

'such stopped vehicles' is the subject (admitted aggregate) at rest, drv.motion.complete_halt (DEF-NRS-484A-260 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not'). 'a clear view ... from a distance of 200 feet in each direction upon such highway' is st.sight_distance at its place, 'the distance along the road within which a vehicle at a point and another vehicle on the road could see each other ... both the view of approaching traffic from that point and its being seen by drivers approaching it, whether or not any road user is there', at least 200 ft. It is not a stand-in for whether an actual road user saw the vehicle (rel.visible): the words require the view to be available, not that anyone is there.

Nearest atoms only, shown to mark the gap: kin.engine_running is 'not a stand-in for motion or a halt'; sig.hazard is a signal, not the vehicle's condition. Neither denotes a disabled vehicle; filed as an atom gap.

Not engaged where the subject is disabled so that it is impossible to avoid stopping (gap).
obligation: st.sight_distance at the subject's place is at least 200 ft. Otherwise violated.

narrowings.why: 'in each direction' is read through the one sight distance of the place, which the atom states for the view of and from traffic approaching it; the two directions are not measured apart.
